# The commands

Every call that reads or changes a database is also a command: a name
and one JSON object, answered by one JSON object. A command is how a
caller that is not a Go program reaches a document. The list is written
from the engine's own table, so it has every command and no other.

One command is answered by more than one object: [`subscribe`](#subscribe)
opens the stream of changes, and its answer is a reply that stays open
and says each event as it is written.

A command reaches a database two ways today. A Go program runs one with
the call `Exec`. And a Go program that has opened a database can let it
answer commands [over HTTP](#over-http), through the package
`fado/httpdoor`. The program `fadodb serve` does that for a database with
users and keys of its own: [Serving a database](serving-a-database.md).

For a program in another language the same list is in
[api/openapi.json](../../api/openapi.json), an OpenAPI document written
from the same table, from which a client is generated.

## A command and its answer

Ann's agent approves an invoice. The command is `transition`, and its
object says which document, which transition and what to write with it:

```json
{"class": "Invoice", "id": "FV/2026/11/0042", "transition": "approve",
 "values": {"note": "matches order PO-118"},
 "key": "approve-FV/2026/11/0042"}
```

The answer holds the document after the command, under `document`:

```json
{"document": {"class": "Invoice", "id": "FV/2026/11/0042", "title": "FV/2026/11/0042",
              "state": "approved", "version": 2, "class_version": 1,
              "created_at": 1794562200, "updated_at": 1794562200, "state_entered_at": 1794562200,
              "created_by": "bob", "updated_by": "ap-agent",
              "state_entered_by": "ap-agent", "state_entered_from": "review",
              "values": {"customer": "Customer:42", "note": "matches order PO-118"}}}
```

When the engine does not carry the command out, the answer holds the
refusal under `error`, with its code, its message and, where there is
one, a hint and the place. Bob, who is not in finance, sends the same
command:

```json
{"error": {"code": "forbidden",
           "message": "bob may not take approve from review",
           "hint": "the rule of approve: INGROUP(\"finance\")",
           "path": "/access/transition/approve"}}
```

[The refusals](refusals.md) lists every code. A definition that is
refused answers `bad_definition`, with every finding beside the error
under `diagnostics`.

## What holds for every command

- **Who calls is never in the command.** The caller comes with the door
  the command is sent through: in a Go program, the principal given to
  `Exec`. The one thing a command says about its caller is `for`, whom
  the caller acts for, and the engine lets that through only while a
  substitution says so.
- **A member the command does not take is refused**, with `bad_json`
  and the place of the member. So is a member given twice, a member of
  the wrong JSON type, and a command that lacks a member it needs. A
  member given as `null` is read as left out.
- **An answer names what it holds**: a document under `document`, a
  list under its plural, a count under its name. A list that is empty is
  `[]`.
- **A definition is read back as it was given.** `get_class`,
  `get_schema`, `get_table` and `get_action` answer the JSON a designer
  wrote under `definition`, with its `name`, its `version` and who
  `defined` it beside it, so that the definition can be changed and sent
  again as it is.

## The members that mean the same everywhere

A command takes the ones its list below shows, and no other.

| Member | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | text | the idempotency key: the same command sent again with the same key makes no second commit and is answered as the first was |
| `business_date` | text | the business day of the commit, as "2026-11-13"; the server's day when left out |
| `reason` | text | why a content administrator acts past a rule of the class; kept on the event |
| `for` | text | the id of whoever the caller acts for; let through only while a substitution says so |
| `at` | moment | the moment the command reads at: "2026-11-13", "2026-11-13 09:30:00" in UTC, or seconds since the epoch; now when left out |

## Documents

| Command | What it does | |
|---|---|---|
| [`create`](#create) | Makes a document. | writes |
| [`create_many`](#create_many) | Makes several documents of one class in one transaction, all or none. | writes |
| [`get`](#get) | Reads a document. | reads |
| [`set`](#set) | Assigns values to a document and recalculates what depends on them. | writes |
| [`reset`](#reset) | Puts input variables of a document back to their defaults. | writes |
| [`refresh`](#refresh) | Recomputes triggered variables of a document, and lets it move if a guard on time now holds. | writes |
| [`transition`](#transition) | Moves a document along a named transition of its class. | writes |
| [`transition_many`](#transition_many) | Moves several documents of one class along one transition; a document that cannot move is reported and the others move. | writes |
| [`delete`](#delete) | Removes a document; its history and its events stay. | destroys |
| [`transitions`](#transitions) | Lists the transitions leaving a document's state, each with whether the caller may take it now. | reads |
| [`due`](#due) | Lists the documents of a class that a commit would move now: a guard on time holds, or a timer has come. | reads |
| [`history`](#history) | Reads every committed version of a document, oldest first. | reads |
| [`version`](#version) | Reads one committed version of a document. | reads |
| [`events`](#events) | Reads the events that touched a document, oldest first. | reads |
| [`subscribe`](#subscribe) | Opens the stream of changes: the caller is told of every event it may read of, in the order of the commits, as each is written. | reads |
| [`preview`](#preview) | Runs a create, a set or a transition without writing anything. | reads |
| [`preview_delete`](#preview_delete) | Answers what a delete of a document would do, without deleting it. | reads |
| [`preview_many`](#preview_many) | Runs the batch transition_many would run, without writing anything. | reads |
| [`query`](#query) | Reads the documents of a class that match a filter. | reads |
| [`count`](#count) | Counts the documents of a class that match a filter. | reads |
| [`flow`](#flow) | Answers the flow of a class: the documents the caller may read in each state now, and their moves along each transition. | reads |
| [`sql`](#sql) | Runs one read-only SELECT over the views, for an analyst. | reads |

### create

Makes a document. It writes; in Go it is the call `Create`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `class` | text | needed | the name of the class |
| `values` | object |  | the values to assign, by variable |
| `id` | text |  | the id of the new document; generated when left out |

And, of the members that mean the same everywhere: `key`, `business_date`, `reason`, `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `document` | the new document |

### subscribe

Opens the stream of changes: the caller is told of every event it may read of, in the order of the commits, as each is written. It reads; in Go it is the call `Subscribe`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `classes` | list of texts |  | the classes to hear of; every class when left out |
| `kinds` | list of texts |  | the kinds of event to hear of, such as created, set and transition; every kind when left out |
| `to_states` | list of texts |  | for a transition, the states entered; every state when left out |
| `after` | text |  | the id of an event: the stream begins after it, so a caller that was away gives the last one it handled; now when left out |

Its answer is a stream and not one object: over HTTP a reply that stays
open and carries one entry for each event, and in Go a value whose
`Next` answers the events one by one. `Exec` answers one object, and
refuses this command with `not_supported`.
[The stream of changes](the-stream-of-changes.md) says what an entry is,
who hears of what and how a stream ends.

### query

Reads the documents of a class that match a filter. It reads; in Go it is the call `Query`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `class` | text | needed | the name of the class |
| `where` | text |  | a formula over the variables of the class; every document when left out |
| `order` | list of texts |  | the variables to sort by, a leading "-" for descending; by id when left out |
| `limit` | whole number |  | the most documents to answer |
| `offset` | whole number |  | how many documents to skip |
| `fields` | list of texts |  | the variables to answer; every one when left out |

And, of the members that mean the same everywhere: `at`, `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `documents` | the documents, in the order asked |

|---|---|---|---|
| `class` | text | needed | the name of the class |
| `where` | text |  | a formula over the variables of the class; every document when left out |

### flow

Answers the flow of a class: the documents the caller may read in each state now, and their moves along each transition. It reads; in Go it is the call `Flow`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `class` | text | needed | the name of the class |
| `since` | moment |  | the first moment of the period the moves and the stays are counted in; since the class began when left out |
| `until` | moment |  | the moment the period ends before; now when left out |

And, of the members that mean the same everywhere: `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `flow` | the states of the class, each with its documents now, since when the oldest is there, and how many stays ended in the period and how long they lasted; and its transitions, each with its moves in the period |

### sql

Runs one read-only SELECT over the views, for an analyst. It reads; in Go it is the call `SQL`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `statement` | text | needed | the SELECT, with ? for each argument |
| `args` | list of values |  | the arguments, in order |

And, of the members that mean the same everywhere: `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `columns` | the names of the columns |
| `rows` | the rows, each a list of values in the order of the columns |

## Definitions

| Command | What it does | |
|---|---|---|
| [`define_class`](#define_class) | Defines a class, or the next version of one. | writes |
| [`define_classes`](#define_classes) | Defines several classes in one call, all or none: how classes that name each other are defined. | writes |
| [`define_schema`](#define_schema) | Defines a named schema of an object. | writes |
| [`define_table`](#define_table) | Defines a table of reference data. | writes |
| [`define_action`](#define_action) | Defines an action a rule may name. | writes |
| [`validate_class`](#validate_class) | Reports what define_class would refuse, storing nothing. | reads |
| [`validate_classes`](#validate_classes) | Reports what define_classes would refuse, storing nothing. | reads |
| [`validate_action`](#validate_action) | Reports what define_action would refuse, storing nothing. | reads |
| [`get_class`](#get_class) | Reads a class back as it was defined. | reads |
| [`get_schema`](#get_schema) | Reads a schema back as it was defined. | reads |
| [`get_table`](#get_table) | Reads a table's definition back as it was defined. | reads |
| [`get_action`](#get_action) | Reads an action's definition back as it was defined. | reads |
| [`list_classes`](#list_classes) | Lists the classes. | reads |
| [`list_schemas`](#list_schemas) | Lists the schemas. | reads |
| [`list_tables`](#list_tables) | Lists the tables. | reads |
| [`list_actions`](#list_actions) | Lists every action a rule may name, the engine's own first. | reads |
| [`definitions`](#definitions) | Lists the versions of one class, schema, table or action, with who defined each and when. | reads |
| [`preview_draft`](#preview_draft) | Tries a class definition that is not stored on a create, or on a document of the stored class of the same name, writing nothing. | reads |
| [`migrate`](#migrate) | Brings every live document of a class that an earlier version computed to the current version. | writes |

### definitions

Lists the versions of one class, schema, table or action, with who defined each and when. It reads; in Go it is the call `Definitions`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `what` | text | needed | class, schema, table or action |
| `name` | text | needed | its name |

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `versions` | the versions, oldest first |

### preview_draft

Tries a class definition that is not stored on a create, or on a document of the stored class of the same name, writing nothing. It reads; in Go it is the call `PreviewDraft`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `definition` | definition | needed | the draft, as JSON |
| `id` | text |  | the id of a document of the stored class; left out, the preview is of a create |
| `values` | object |  | the values to assign, by variable |
| `transition` | text |  | the name of a transition to take |

And, of the members that mean the same everywhere: `reason`, `at`, `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `preview` | what the command would do: the document as it would be, the errors, the states visited, the transitions then open and the rules that would run |

### migrate

Brings every live document of a class that an earlier version computed to the current version. It writes; in Go it is the call `Migrate`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `class` | text | needed | the name of the class |

And, of the members that mean the same everywhere: `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `migrated` | how many documents it moved |

## Tables, actions and the queue

| Command | What it does | |
|---|---|---|
| [`table_rows`](#table_rows) | Reads every row of a table, in the order of its key. | reads |
| [`import_rows`](#import_rows) | Writes rows into a table; a row whose key exists is replaced. | writes |
| [`preview_action`](#preview_action) | Answers what an action would be called with, or the request it would send, with every secret masked; nothing is called or sent. | reads |
| [`try_action`](#try_action) | Runs an action once, outside any document; a request is sent for real. | writes |
| [`outbox`](#outbox) | Lists the actions commits queued: what waits, what ran and what is dead. | reads |
| [`retry_action`](#retry_action) | Makes a dead action pending again. | writes |
| [`drain`](#drain) | Runs every queued action that is due, now. | writes |
| [`check_blobs`](#check_blobs) | Recomputes the hash of every file the database holds, and looks for every file a document holds. | reads |

### table_rows

Reads every row of a table, in the order of its key. It reads; in Go it is the call `TableRows`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `table` | text | needed | the name of the table |

And, of the members that mean the same everywhere: `at`, `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `rows` | the rows, each an object of values by column |

### import_rows

Writes rows into a table; a row whose key exists is replaced. It writes; in Go it is the call `ImportRows`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `table` | text | needed | the name of the table |
| `rows` | list of objects | needed | the rows, each an object of values by column |
| `replace` | true or false |  | true empties the table first, so that the rows given are all its rows |

And, of the members that mean the same everywhere: `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `imported` | how many rows it wrote |

### preview_action

Answers what an action would be called with, or the request it would send, with every secret masked; nothing is called or sent. It reads; in Go it is the call `PreviewAction`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | text | needed | the name of the action |
| `args` | object |  | its arguments, by parameter |

And, of the members that mean the same everywhere: `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `preview` | the call, or the request |

### try_action

Runs an action once, outside any document; a request is sent for real. It writes; in Go it is the call `TryAction`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | text | needed | the name of the action |
| `args` | object |  | its arguments, by parameter |

And, of the members that mean the same everywhere: `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `outcome` | what the action returned, or how it failed |

### outbox

Lists the actions commits queued: what waits, what ran and what is dead. It reads; in Go it is the call `Outbox`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | text |  | pending, done or dead; every status when left out |
| `class` | text |  | only the actions of documents of this class |
| `id` | text |  | only the actions of this document |
| `limit` | whole number |  | the most actions to answer |

And, of the members that mean the same everywhere: `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `actions` | the actions, in the order they were queued |

### retry_action

Makes a dead action pending again. It writes; in Go it is the call `RetryAction`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action_key` | text | needed | the key of the queued action, as outbox lists it |

And, of the members that mean the same everywhere: `for`.

It answers `{}`.

### drain

Runs every queued action that is due, now. It writes; in Go it is the call `Drain`.

It takes nothing of its own; of the members that mean the same everywhere, `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `attempted` | how many actions it attempted |

### check_blobs

Recomputes the hash of every file the database holds, and looks for every file a document holds. It reads; in Go it is the call `CheckBlobs`.

It takes nothing of its own; of the members that mean the same everywhere, `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `checked` | how many files it checked |
| `mismatched` | the hashes of the files whose bytes do not match |
| `missing` | the files a document holds, in any version, that the database has lost, each {"hash", "class", "id", "version", "variable"} |

## Users, groups and keys

A database that a server opens for callers of its own keeps who they
are: its users, their groups and their keys. A user is a person, an
agent or a service the database knows by its id. A group is a name on
a user. A key is how a user proves who it is: one line of text that
begins `fado_`, shown once when it is made and kept nowhere after.

These commands are offered by such a database only. A database opened
by a program that says itself who is calling keeps no users, and
answers each of them with `unknown_command`. The server `fadodb serve` opens its
database this way, and a Go program does with `Options.Users`.

| Command | What it does | |
|---|---|---|
| [`create_user`](#create_user) | Makes a user: a person, an agent or a service the database knows by its id. It is a database administrator's. | writes |
| [`set_user`](#set_user) | Changes a user: the members given, and no other. It is a database administrator's, who may change their own groups too. | writes |
| [`get_user`](#get_user) | Reads one user. Every user may ask. | reads |
| [`list_users`](#list_users) | Lists the users, in the order of their ids. Every user may ask. | reads |
| [`user_changes`](#user_changes) | Lists every change to a user and to its keys. A database administrator may ask of any user, and a user of itself. | reads |
| [`create_key`](#create_key) | Makes a key for a user and answers it with its secret, this once. It is a database administrator's. | writes |
| [`list_keys`](#list_keys) | Lists the keys of a user, never a secret. A database administrator may ask of any user, and a user of itself. | reads |
| [`revoke_key`](#revoke_key) | Ends a key: the next command sent with it is refused. A database administrator may revoke any key, and a user its own. | writes |
| [`whoami`](#whoami) | Answers who the database takes the caller for. | reads |

### create_user

Makes a user: a person, an agent or a service the database knows by its id. It is a database administrator's. It writes; in Go it is the call `CreateUser`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | text | needed | the id every event will record; it never changes and is never given to somebody else |
| `kind` | text | needed | person, agent or service |
| `name` | text |  | how a screen shows the user |
| `groups` | list of texts |  | the groups of the user, which INGROUP answers |
| `system_groups` | list of texts |  | the system groups of the user: administrators, designers, content-administrators, analysts |

And, of the members that mean the same everywhere: `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `user` | the user: its id, its kind, its name, its groups, its system groups and whether it is disabled |

### set_user

Changes a user: the members given, and no other. It is a database administrator's, who may change their own groups too. It writes; in Go it is the call `SetUser`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | text | needed | the id of the user |
| `name` | text |  | how a screen shows the user |
| `groups` | list of texts |  | the groups of the user, in place of the ones it has |
| `system_groups` | list of texts |  | the system groups of the user, in place of the ones it has |
| `disabled` | true or false |  | true stops every key of the user at the next command; false lets them through again |

And, of the members that mean the same everywhere: `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `user` | the user: its id, its kind, its name, its groups, its system groups and whether it is disabled, after the change |

### get_user

Reads one user. Every user may ask. It reads; in Go it is the call `GetUser`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | text | needed | the id of the user |

And, of the members that mean the same everywhere: `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `user` | the user: its id, its kind, its name, its groups, its system groups and whether it is disabled |

### list_users

Lists the users, in the order of their ids. Every user may ask. It reads; in Go it is the call `Users`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `group` | text |  | only the members of this group, of either kind |
| `kind` | text |  | only the users of this kind |

And, of the members that mean the same everywhere: `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `users` | the users, the disabled ones among them |

### user_changes

Lists every change to a user and to its keys. A database administrator may ask of any user, and a user of itself. It reads; in Go it is the call `UserChanges`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | text | needed | the id of the user |

And, of the members that mean the same everywhere: `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `changes` | the changes, oldest first: what was done, by whom, of what kind, for whom and when, with the user or the key as the change left it |

### create_key

Makes a key for a user and answers it with its secret, this once. It is a database administrator's. It writes; in Go it is the call `CreateKey`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `user` | text | needed | the id of the user the key is for |
| `label` | text |  | where the key is used, such as laptop or nightly import |
| `expires` | text |  | the last day the key holds, as YYYY-MM-DD in UTC; left out, the key holds until it is revoked |

And, of the members that mean the same everywhere: `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `key` | the key: its id, its user, its label, when and by whom it was made, its last day, and under secret the key itself, which is shown this once and kept nowhere |

### list_keys

Lists the keys of a user, never a secret. A database administrator may ask of any user, and a user of itself. It reads; in Go it is the call `Keys`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `user` | text |  | the id of the user; left out, the caller |

And, of the members that mean the same everywhere: `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `keys` | the keys, oldest first, the revoked ones among them |

### revoke_key

Ends a key: the next command sent with it is refused. A database administrator may revoke any key, and a user its own. It writes; in Go it is the call `RevokeKey`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | text | needed | the id of the key, as list_keys shows it, and not the key itself |

And, of the members that mean the same everywhere: `for`.

It answers `{}`.

### whoami

Answers who the database takes the caller for. It reads; in Go it is the call `Whoami`.

It takes nothing of its own; of the members that mean the same everywhere, `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `user` | the user: its id, its kind, its name, its groups, its system groups and whether it is disabled |
| `for` | the id of whoever the caller acts for, when the command names one |

## Over HTTP

A Go program that has opened a database lets it answer commands over
HTTP with the package `fado/httpdoor`. The program says where it listens
and who sends each request, and the door does the rest. One door serves
one database.

A command is sent to the address that ends in its name, with `POST`,
its object as the body and the header `Content-Type: application/json`.
The answer is the body of the reply. A command that reads is a `POST`
too.

```
POST /v1/transition
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer …

{"class": "Invoice", "id": "FV/2026/11/0042", "transition": "approve"}
```

- **Who sends the request is not in the command**, here either. The
  program that makes the door gives it a function that reads who it is
  from the request: from a session or a token of the program's own. A
  request whose sender the function cannot tell is refused with
  `unauthenticated`, in the same words whatever was wrong, and runs
  nothing. A database that keeps its own
  [users, groups and keys](#users-groups-and-keys) gives the door
  `httpdoor.Keys`: a request then carries a key of a user, as the
  header `Authorization: Bearer fado_…`, and nothing else is a
  credential.
- **The id of a document travels in the JSON** and never in the
  address, so an id such as `FV/2026/11/0042` needs no escaping.
- **A door takes on so much and no more.** Unless the program says
  otherwise: a request of at most 16 MiB, refused beyond that with
  `too_large`; a command that runs at most 30 seconds, stopped after
  that and refused with `timeout`; and 64 commands at once. A request
  beyond them waits one second for a command to end and is then refused
  with `busy`; nothing of it ran, and it can be sent again.
- **One command is answered with a stream.** `POST /v1/subscribe` opens
  the stream of changes: the reply has the status 200 and the kind
  `text/event-stream`, stays open, and carries one entry for each event
  the caller may read of. A door holds 256 of them open unless the
  program says otherwise, and refuses one beyond them with `busy`, at
  once. [The stream of changes](the-stream-of-changes.md) has the rest.
- **A request that is not a command as JSON is told so.** One that is
  not a `POST` is answered with the status 405, and a body that is not
  said to be JSON with 415. Both carry the code `bad_json` and a hint.
  So does a request with members in its address, such as `?limit=10`:
  they belong in the object.
- **A caller reads the code, not the status.** The status of a reply
  is worked out from its code, for the proxies and the tools between
  the caller and the door:

  | Status | Codes |
  |---|---|
  | 200 | the command ran |
  | 400 | `bad_json` |
  | 401 | `unauthenticated` |
  | 403 | `forbidden`, `reason_required` |
  | 404 | `unknown_class`, `unknown_document`, `unknown_table`, `unknown_schema`, `unknown_blob`, `unknown_action`, `unknown_row`, `unknown_user`, `unknown_key`, `unknown_command` |
  | 409 | `key_reused`, `duplicate`, `terminal`, `wrong_state`, `guard_false` |
  | 413 | `blob_too_large`, `too_large` |
  | 422 | every other refusal |
  | 500 | `storage`, `internal` |
  | 503 | `closed`, `busy` |
  | 504 | `timeout` |

### Files over HTTP

The bytes of a file are not JSON, so they travel beside the commands,
at three addresses of their own. What a file is on a document, its
facts, is a value like any other and travels in the commands;
[Files](files.md) says how.

| Address | Does | Answers |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /v1/blobs?name=taxi.pdf` | keeps the bytes of the body under their hash, with the `Content-Type` of the request as their kind | `{"file": {"hash": …, "name": …, "media_type": …, "size": …}}`: the facts to set on a document, in a command |
| `GET /v1/file?class=Receipt&id=R-7&hash=d694…` | streams a file the document holds at its current version, or at the one `version=` names; `for=` says for whom the caller acts | the bytes |
| `GET /v1/blob?hash=d694…` | streams bytes by their hash alone, for a content administrator | the bytes |

- **A file is read under the rules of its document.** A caller who may
  not read the document is answered `unknown_document`, and one who may
  not read the variable that holds the file is answered `unknown_blob`:
  what is hidden is absent.
- **A parameter the address does not take is refused**, with
  `bad_json`, as a member of a command is, and so is one given twice. A
  value is escaped: `id=FV%2F2026%2F11%2F0042`.
- **The body of a put is the bytes themselves.** A form is refused.
  A file larger than the database keeps is refused with
  `blob_too_large`.
- **A browser is told to save the file and not to show it**, whatever
  kind the one who put it said it is.
- **The hash is the tag of the bytes**, sent as `ETag`. A caller that
  holds them and sends the tag back in `If-None-Match` is answered with
  the status 304 and no bytes, after the engine has checked once more
  that the caller may read the file.
- **A file in transfer holds the place of a command**, and is not
  stopped by the time one command may run.

## What is not a command

A few calls of the Go package have no command.

| Call | Why |
|---|---|
| `Action` | it answers one entry of the catalogue that list_actions answers whole |
| `Authenticate` | it answers who a key belongs to, for the door that is given the key; a caller that wants to know who it is sends whoami |
| `Class` | it answers the engine's compiled form to a Go program; get_class answers the definition |
| `Close` | closing a database is for the program that opened it |
| `Exec` | it is the door the commands come through |
| `OpenBlob` | the bytes of a file are not JSON: they travel beside the commands, with the server |
| `OpenFile` | the bytes of a file are not JSON: they travel beside the commands, with the server |
| `OutboxCounts` | it counts what of the queue is still to do, for whoever watches a server, which answers it at GET /v1/metrics; outbox lists the actions themselves |
| `Ping` | it asks whether the database answers; a server answers it at GET /v1/health, for anybody |
| `PutBlob` | the bytes of a file are not JSON: they travel beside the commands, with the server |
| `Schema` | it answers the engine's compiled form to a Go program; get_schema answers the definition |
| `Table` | it answers the engine's compiled form to a Go program; get_table answers the definition |
